author: Alex Daniel
description:
Government spending watchdog warns of price of keeping publicly owned firm in business

Labour has been urged to lay out a credible plan for the future of British Steel, as the government spending watchdog warned of the “startling” costs of keeping the struggling manufacturer in business with no end in sight.

British Steel was taken into public ownership in July to protect “the future of steel production”, 15 months after the government stepped in to prevent the closure of its steelworks in Scunthorpe and the loss of 4,000 jobs.

Continue reading...
title: Find a credible plan for British Steel, ministers told as ‘startling’ costs soar

author: Rajeev Syal Home affairs editor
description:
Shabana Mahmood says she wants to distinguish between far-right extremism and legitimate local concerns over asylum sites

Shabana Mahmood has described the anti-asylum activist Daniel Thomas as “a far-right and outright racist” who will feel “the full force of the law” if his organisation commits crimes near contested asylum sites such as Piddington.

In an interview with the Guardian, the home secretary also “wanted to reassure” concerned villagers that asylum seekers due to move in to a neighbouring former defence site would not “put pressure” on local resources because they would be given “self-contained facilities”.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Outright racist’ activist Daniel Thomas will face ‘full force of law’ over any crimes, says home secretary

author: Associated Press
description:
Anthony Kazmierczak agreed plea deal over January town-hall attack that came amid Minneapolis ICE crackdown

The man who sprayed vinegar at the Democratic US House member Ilhan Omar during a Minneapolis town hall was sentenced Thursday to 14 months in prison after reaching a deal with prosecutors.

The sentencing of 56-year-old Anthony Kazmierczak came nearly eight months after the 27 January assault. At the time, Minneapolis was facing an immigration crackdown that led to angry protests, arrests and the killing of two US citizens by federal officers.

Continue reading...
title: Man who sprayed Ilhan Omar with vinegar sentenced to 14 months

author: Martin Farrer
description:
Follow the day’s news live.

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Kurt Campbell, chairman of the Asia Group and formerly the national security coordinator for the Indo-Pacific in the Biden administration, told a US thinktank that US willingness to work with allies “occasionally is lost” but that he hoped for a return to a more globally engaged America.

The CSIS event marked five years since the announcement of the Aukus pact between the US, UK and Australia.

I believe that this enduring quality of American diplomacy will see a brighter day again.

I would simply say that the idea that we will enhance our security by withdrawing from allies and partners is deeply, profoundly misguided. And we hav
title: Australia news live: Albanese to meet Apple’s Tim Cook in US after social media reform; Burke defends immigration policy

author: Patrick Daly
description:
HMRC wins challenge over John Griffin’s claim to be non-dom despite having lived in England since childhood

The founder of Addison Lee owes £20.5m in tax after a tribunal dismissed a claim that he should be treated as a nom-dom despite living in the UK since childhood.

John Griffin had argued he should be treated as a nom-dom due to his connection to Ireland, saying: “I was and am besotted with Ireland, infatuated with Ireland. I believe that I have always been and am Irish.”

Continue reading...
title: Addison Lee founder owes £20.5m in tax after UK tribunal ruling

author: Emine Sinmaz
description:
Exclusive: Sisters of Nicholas Brandram recount 44-year-old’s deteriorating mental health in days before he took his life

Days before Nicholas Brandram, the man suspected of being the “Putney pusher”, killed himself, he told his family that the police investigation was “murdering him”.

He had “no fight left” in him, he told his sisters, Alexia Hicks and Sophie Voelcker, and could not see an end to the Metropolitan police investigation, or the online abuse.

Continue reading...
title: Suspect in ‘Putney pusher’ case told family that investigation was ‘murdering him’

author: Marina Dunbar
description:
Students required to disclose information if they wish to make up swimming days lost because of their periods

A Michigan high school is facing scrutiny after parents raised concerns over a gym class policy requiring female students to disclose information about their menstrual cycles if they want to make up swimming days missed because of their periods.

Under the policy, which appears in a Lakeview high school gym syllabus, female students who miss swimming because of their periods must have a parent submit a written note or email identifying the length of their menstrual cycle before they can make up the missed days.

Continue reading...
title: Outcry as Michigan high school asks girls to share details of menstrual cycles

author: Ariana Baio
description:
Critics had criticized administration for nominating Schroyer, who has no formal experience working in ICE

The White House has withdrawn the nomination of former Oklahoma state trooper Lance Schroyer to head Immigration and Customs Enforcement, less than three months after announcing his role.

Critics had initially criticized administration officials for nominating Schroyer, who has no formal experience working in ICE. Schroyer previously worked as a member of homeland security secretary Markwayne Mullin’s security detail when he was in the Senate.

Continue reading...
title: White House withdraws nomination of ex-state trooper Lance Schroyer to head ICE

author: Chris Stein in Washington
description:
The Arizona senator shepherded the confirmation of conservative supreme court justice Brett Kavanaugh

Jon Kyl, a Republican former US senator from Arizona who shepherded conservative supreme court justice Brett Kavanaugh through his confirmation hearing, died on Thursday at 84, his family announced.

The cause was complications from a neurological disease, according to a statement. Last December, Kyl announced that he had been diagnosed with dementia.

Continue reading...
title: Jon Kyl, former Republican US senator who served three terms, dies aged 84

author: Lucy Campbell
description:
Attorney also said Elizabeth Siders, 34, had been almost continuously pregnant since age 15 without regular healthcare

An Ohio mother whose 16 children were rescued from appalling conditions pleaded not guilty to child endangerment and neglect charges in court on Wednesday.

Elizabeth Siders, 34, is one of four family members, including her husband, Gary Siders Jr, charged with 16 charges of child endangerment and neglect after investigators found the children, who were 17 months to 18 years old, in “deplorable conditions” at the decrepit family home in the tiny village of Hamden in July.

Continue reading...
title: Ohio mom with 16 kids rescued from ‘deplorable’ conditions pleads not guilty to child neglect

author: Presented by Lucy Hough with Jon Henley; producer Angus Neale; senior producer Ryan Ramgobin; executive producer Zoe Hitch
description:
Canadian prime minister, Mark Carney, has welcomed the EU’s proposal for Canada to become the bloc’s first ‘associate member’, despite threats from Donald Trump over the plan. The US president said Washington could impose ‘very serious tariffs’ or halt trade if the EU went ahead with the plan. But in a defiant speech to the European parliament, Carney called for ‘deep cooperation’ and said polling showed the overwhelming majority of Canadians supported closer ties with Europe. Lucy Hough speaks to Europe correspondent Jon Henley – watch on YouTube

Continue reading...
title: Taking on Trump: Canada and EU forge closer ties – The Latest

author: Marina Dunbar
description:
State reportedly asks for Epi-Aid support unless federal agency recognizes four local measles-related deaths

Pennsylvania is seeking emergency assistance from the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) as a major measles outbreak spreads across the state. The state warned the request could be withdrawn unless the federal agency publicly recognizes four measles-associated deaths reported by the state.

The Pennsylvania department of health has begun the process of requesting CDC emergency support known as an Epi-Aid, Reuters reported on Thursday.
title: Pennsylvania asks CDC for emergency help as measles outbreak spreads

author: Chris Stein
description:
María Elvira Salazar says some enforcement has ‘gone too far’ as GOP seeks distance from Trump before midterms

A Republican congresswoman has released a campaign ad criticizing Donald Trump’s approach to immigration enforcement, in the latest sign that a key plank of the president’s 2024 re-election campaign has become a liability for his congressional allies ahead of November’s midterm elections.

“Mr President, some of your immigration enforcement efforts have gone too far,” Florida’s María Elvira Salazar says in a 30-second ad. “In July, 50% of the 50,000 people that were detained had no criminal record. Be careful
title: House Republican releases campaign ad critical of Trump’s immigration policies

author: Patrick Commins
description:
The country’s migration settings have become a source of discontent – but will Tony Burke’s approach be seen as the right mix?

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Tony Burke has promised to make Labor’s existing migration policy work better rather than announcing a dramatic cut in numbers, arguing that populist promises to slash net overseas migration will “trash Australian services and trash the Australian economy”.

The home affairs minister’s message was immediately endorsed by employer groups, who over recent days have made it clear that steps to arbitrarily slash migrant numbers would compound already severe skills shortages and hurt businesses, especially those in the regions.
title: Amid claims of ‘mass migration’, Labor hopes a measured approach will take the hot air out of the debate

author: Tom McIlroy and Luca Ittimani
description:
Farming lobby says shoppers will see emptier shelves and higher prices because of restrictions on backpackers

  • Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

The farming lobby’s claim that immigration rule changes will increase food prices for households is wrong, Tony Burke has said, describing moves to speed up processing of backpacker visas as a positive step for agriculture.

Burke unveiled Labor’s long-awaited reforms at the National Press Club on Thursday, flagging that the plan was more limited than the government would like, due to a lack of support for wider legislation from the Coalition.
title: Tony Burke rejects farmers’ claims that immigration changes will increase food prices

author: Caroline Davies
description:
From ‘there were three of us in this marriage’ to ‘recollections may vary’, a lot can be conveyed with a carefully worded phrase

As denials go, King Charles’s response to Earl Spencer’s allegations that Charles said after Diana’s death “We’ll forget her soon enough” was a masterclass in the diplomatic royal rebuke.

Rarely has Buckingham Palace responded to claims in countless books on royalty. But it was straight out of the block on this one.

Continue reading...
title: As Charles refutes Earl Spencer’s claim about Diana, how royal statements give a glimpse behind palace doors

author: Ariana Baio
description:
National Park Service lays out concerns that planned 250ft arch could interfere with historic sites in US capital

Donald Trump’s desired triumphal arch in downtown Washington DC will likely contribute “to adverse effects to historic properties”, per the National Park Service’s planning document, but the construction is still planned to go forward.

The president’s 250ft arch could interfere with some of the most well-known views in the nation’s capital, including the symbolic relationship between Arlington House, Arlington National Cemetery, Arlington Memorial Bridge and the Lincoln Memorial, which face each other to represent the reunification of the United States after the civil war.

Contin
title: Trump arch could have ‘adverse effects’ on nearby DC monuments, US park service says

author: Sam Levin in Los Angeles
description:
Exclusive: Internal FBI memo, reviewed by the Guardian, said women wanted to dox and ‘embarrass’ agents, but provided few details

The FBI internally warned that a group of women were creating fake online dating accounts with “tradwife” aesthetics in an effort to lure US immigration agents and “dox” them.

The FBI in Chicago disseminated a brief memo to other law enforcement officials across the US on the potential threat to agents in February, warning that “as of late January 2026, a small group of women allegedly were creating fictitious online dating profiles with the purpose of attracting and then doxxing law enforcement participating in immigration enforcement”. The report, which was shared with the Guardian, provided few details about the alleged scheme and did not explain the source of the information.

Continue reading...
title: FBI warned ICE agents could be targeted by fake ‘tradwife’ dating profiles, memo reveals

author: Nicola Slawson and Jane Clinton
description:
As concern about loneliness and social isolation grows, we spoke to people who have joined groups and set up activities

Amid growing concern about loneliness and social isolation, new research from the Institute for Public Policy Research found the number of young people in England with no close friends has risen fivefold since 2014, with one in 20 now reporting having none at all.

Making new friends as an adult is not always easy. We spoke to people who have taken deliberate steps to make new connections about what worked for them.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Amazing community’: how people are making new friends and connections as adults

author: Bethan McKernan Wales correspondent
description:
Community groups and schools work with Wales’s folk arts organisation to set stories of the area’s people to music

Growing up in Wales, Liz Puleston-Jones was familiar with the country’s rich heritage of storytelling and traditional music, but none of it ever seemed to have much of a connection to her life in Swansea.

Researching the history of the area as part of Cân y Cymoedd (When Valleys Sing), a project in nearby Port Talbot, she came across the story of Isabel Thomas, a 14-year-old girl in the 1940s who left school and lied about her age to work in a tin plate works to support her family.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Songwriting instead of doomscrolling’: project inspires Port Talbot to tune into its heritage

author: Anna Betts
description:
It is the second year this administration has barred the Palestinian delegation from US travel ahead of the forum

The US state department said on Wednesday that it had again denied entry visas to Palestinian officials ahead next week’s United Nations general assembly gathering in New York.

The state department said in a statement that the Palestinian Authority (PA) and the Palestine Liberation Organization (PLO) had “failed to live up to their commitments”, accusing the groups of “taking actions to internationalize the Israeli-Palestinian Conflict including through the International Criminal Court (ICC) and International Court of Justice (ICJ)” and of “glorifying terrori
title: Trump administration denies entry visas to Palestinian officials ahead of UN general assembly

author: Helena Horton
description:
Rhys Woods says there are ‘no words’ for family’s pain after Noah’s body was found in pond near Suffolk playground

The father of Noah, the three-year-old boy who was found dead after going missing from a playground, has spoken of his heartbreak and thanked the community who launched a tireless search for his son.

Rhys Woods said there were “no words to describe the pain of this loss”, adding that the family was “absolutely heartbroken”.

Continue reading...
title: Father of Noah, three, thanks those who searched for his son as village reels from loss

author: Reuters
description:
Christian Castro faced assault charges after shooting Venezuelan man through the door of his apartment while children were present

A federal immigration officer wanted on assault charges for shooting and ​wounding a Venezuelan man in Minneapolis was arrested there on Wednesday, eight months after a confrontation that became a flashpoint over ‌Donald Trump’s deportation sweeps.

Christian Castro, an Immigrations and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agent, was taken into custody by agents of the Minnesota Bureau of Criminal Apprehension in Minneapolis and was booked into the Hennepin county jail on his outstanding arrest warrant, the agency said.

Continue reading...
title: ICE agent arrested in Minneapolis on charges of assault and false reporting of crime

author: Heather Stewart
description:
PM’s push to cut cost of living is threatened by rising inflation and higher government borrowing costs

  • Bank of England holds interest rates

  • Business live – latest updates

Good luck to Andy Burnham convincing voters he is giving them “breathing space,” if the Bank of England ratchets up interest rates in the coming months.

That was the prospect opened up by Thursday’s minutes of the Bank’s monetary policy committee (MPC) meeting, which left rates unchanged at 3.75% – for now – but suggested policymakers may be unlikely to hold out much longer.
title: Burnham has to sell Bank rate rises as ‘breathing space’ – good luck with that

author: Vivian Ho
description:
Canada’s prime minister, Mark Carney, is due to address the European parliament on Thursday. Plus, how the attention economy overwhelmed children’s TV

Good morning.

Donald Trump has threatened the EU with “serious tariffs” after the European Commission president, Ursula von der Leyen, invited Canada to become the EU’s first “associate member”.

Why does the EU want closer ties with Canada? Von der Leyen told the European parliament that, as democracies faced a “fracture in the international rules-based system”, Brussels and Ottawa needed to pull closer together. “This is a partnership not against anyone else, but for our common strength,” she said.

How has the EU responded to Trump’s comments? France’s Europe minister, Benjamin Haddad, said on Thursday that Washington had no power to veto
title: Trump threatens EU with tariffs over membership offer to Canada | First Thing

author: Jessica Glenza
description:
Shutdown of study is latest for Trump administration, which has canceled, frozen and otherwise disrupted more than 5,700 medical research grants over two years

Scientific funding cuts imposed by the Trump administration may force researchers to close a study on Alzheimer’s disease risk among 600 ageing people without sharing the results of cognitive tests with participants – even though researchers have all the data to do so.

The Trump administration canceled a federal research grant studying two low-income, majority Black neighborhoods in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, in August. Researchers were given 90 days to shut down the study – more than five months earlier than planned. Now, they lack the time and money to assess data collected from trial participants.
title: Hundreds of ageing Americans may not get results of Alzheimer’s study due to Trump cuts

author: Kalyeena Makortoff Banking correspondent
description:
Union calls for payouts to help cover travel costs and exemption for those living more than 40 minutes away

  • Business live – latest updates

Barclays is facing a growing backlash over return-to-office plans, with thousands of staff calling for payouts to help cover travel costs and an exemption for those living more than 40 minutes from work.

Unionised staff represented by Unite are pushing back against plans announced by the bank earlier this summer to get staff back into the office at least three days a week from October, with more senior employees expected to come in at least four days a week.

Continue reading...
title: Thousands of Barclays staff revolt over return-to-office mandate

author: Andrew Sparrow
description:
The Conservatives want to brand Burnham’s administration as a ‘traditional tax and spend socialist government’

Good morning. With less than six weeks so go until the budget, economics is rising up the agenda at Westminster. The Bank of England is announcing its latest interest rate decision later – Graeme Wearden will have all the details on his business live blog – and Andrew Griffith is giving his first major speech since being appointed as shadow chancellor just over two weeks ago.

Not surprisingly, Griffith is urging the chancellor, John Healey, to rule out tax rises in the budget. He has been doing interviews this morning and he told BBC Breakfast:

The taxes or the fear of taxes … are driving really big taxpayers to leave our country for overseas, taking hundr
title: Tories challenge chancellor to rule out tax rises in budget – UK politics live

author: Australian Associated Press
description:
Court hears Mauro Paul Coluzzi and two associates defrauded customers and banks of more than $130,000

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

An Australia Post worker’s crippling gambling addiction spiralled into purchases of gold jewellery, phones and even online gaming gift cards with stolen bank cards.

Mauro Paul Coluzzi’s family members broke down in court as he was jailed until December 2027 for leading two criminal syndicates funded with pilfered plastic.
title: Australia Post worker stole dozens of bank cards to fund ‘debilitating’ gambling addiction

author: Rob Davies
description:
Lords’ report faces criticism from lobby groups after suggesting ban would be ‘most effective’ way to reduce public harms

The UK should introduce a ban on almost all gambling advertising to protect public health, a cross-party group of peers has urged, prompting fury from the lobby group for bookmakers and casinos.

In a 173-page report, the House of Lords liaison committee said the government had been “too passive” in response to an explosion of digital advertising and social media influencers promoting the gambling sector.

Continue reading...
title: Peers call for UK to enact tobacco-style ban on gambling advertising

author: Libby Brooks
description:
In today’s newsletter: The Houthi advance along the Red Sea coast raised fears for global trade and energy supplies, while more than 100,000 Yemenis have been displaced by the fighting

Good morning. The lightning advance of Houthi militants along the west coast of Yemen over the past week has prompted fears of a spiralling conflict in the region and a new oil supply crisis.

For families living in the Middle East’s poorest country, the most significant fighting between the Iran-aligned Houthis and the Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces in years is a crisis upon a catastrophe, with escalating civilian casualties and at least 100,000 displaced in recent days.

UK politics | Key allies of Andy Burnham have warned the prime minister not to back down over his promises to put water companies under public
title: Thursday briefing: Yemen’s war continues to threaten oil supplies– but what about its people?

author: Amanda Meade
description:
Former 2GB and 2UE broadcaster has pleaded not guilty to 22 indecent assault and sexual touching charges

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

An alleged victim of Alan Jones has told a Sydney court that an unwanted kiss from the former shock jock more than a decade ago is seared in his memory and he wished it never happened.

The ex-sportsman, known as complainant M, agreed during cross-examination by the defence that he sent Jones a shirtless photo of him in Paris some months before the alleged kiss.
title: Prominent athlete tells Alan Jones trial he sent shirtless photo before unwanted kiss he wished ‘never happened’

author: David Smith in Gastonia, North Carolina and Lauren Gambino
description:
President stumps for Senate nominee Michael Whatley in North Carolina and urges voters to ‘crush the communists’

Donald Trump returned to the campaign trail on Wednesday, imploring North Carolina voters to “pretend I’m on the ticket” and “crush the communists” in the November elections at a rally in support of the Republican Senate nominee Michael Whatley.

Despite Trump’s deep unpopularity, Republicans hope to once again turn the president’s loyal following into a political force as the party confronts an unforgiving midterm landscape.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Pretend I’m on the ticket’: Trump hits campaign trail in bid to boost Republican hopes

author: Krishani Dhanji
description:
Independent senator had denounced as ‘cruel’ the plan to impose a $5,000 cap on allied health services for veterans

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Labor has backed down on plans to impose a $5,000 cap on health services for defence veterans, caving to growing political pressure after weeks of criticism.

The government announced it would no longer pursue the cap for allied health services, which had been to come into force on 1 July 2027, after a weeks-long campaign by the opposition, veterans’ groups and
title: Labor backs down on veterans’ health services cap after furious backlash from Jacqui Lambie and ex-ADF members
